title: New York Times AI Hallucination Correction: AI-Generated Quotation
description: The New York Times issued an editors' note after learning that a remark attributed to Pierre Poilievre was actually an AI-generated summary of his views that AI rendered as a quotation. The article now accurately quotes from his April speech. Highlights the challenge of AI hallucinations in journalism.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Changelog: Intent, Amelia Wattenberger, and the agent-first redesign of developer tools
description: Amelia Wattenberger discusses designing Intent at Augment Code in an agent-first world. Key insight: 'the last 30% of any software project is about to become the hardest part you've ever done.' Covers the identity crisis developers face as agents take over the keyboard, epic redesign of developer tooling, and tradeoffs between one-worktree-per-agent vs one-worktree-per-task.
author: The Changelog

title: OpenAI's WebRTC Problem: Low Latency vs Prompt Accuracy
description: Luke Curley discusses how WebRTC degrades and drops audio packets during poor network conditions. For conference calls this makes sense, but for LLM voice interactions where users pay for accurate responses, it's problematic. There's no way to wait for retransmission in WebRTC - the implementation is hard-coded for real-time latency above all else.
author: Simon Willison (citing Luke Curley)

title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
description: Thariq Shihipar advocates for HTML over Markdown as an output format for Claude. HTML enables SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, in-page navigation, and richer explanations. Simon tested this by having GPT-5.5 create an HTML explanation of the copy.fail Linux security exploit, demonstrating how HTML can create rich, interactive technical documentation.
author: Simon Willison

title: How Anthropic's Mythos has rewritten Firefox's approach to cybersecurity
description: TechCrunch covers how Mozilla used Claude Mythos to dramatically scale up vulnerability discovery in Firefox, going from 20-30 bugs per month to 423 in April. Explores the transformational impact on Mozilla's security processes and the broader implications for AI-assisted security research.
author: Russell Brandom

title: The Changelog: Astral joins OpenAI, and the future of developer tools
description: Discussion of Astral joining OpenAI, signaling where the center of gravity is moving for developer tools. Also covers LiteLLM supply-chain attack, OpenCode as an open-source coding agent stack, Rust's public reality check on pain points, and Ryan Lizza using AI to build an open-source TurboTax alternative.
author: The Changelog

title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
description: Mozilla used access to Claude Mythos preview to locate and fix hundreds of vulnerabilities in Firefox. They went from fixing 20-30 security bugs per month to 423 in April 2026 alone. The key was improved techniques for harnessing models - steering them, scaling them, and stacking them to generate signal and filter noise.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cloudflare says AI made 1,100 jobs obsolete, even as revenue hit a record high
description: Cloudflare revealed that AI automation eliminated 1,100 positions while the company achieved record revenue. Raises important questions about AI's impact on employment and the economic dynamics of AI-driven efficiency gains.
author: Julie Bort

title: Notes on the xAI/Anthropic data center deal
description: Anthropic struck a deal with SpaceX/xAI to use 'all of the capacity of their Colossus data center'. This was one of the biggest announcements from Anthropic's Code w/ Claude 2026 event, representing a significant infrastructure partnership.
author: Simon Willison

title: Vibe coding and agentic engineering are getting closer than I'd like
description: Simon discusses his disturbing realization that vibe coding and agentic engineering have started to converge in his own work. From conversation with Joseph Ruscio on Heavybit's High Leverage podcast about AI coding tools and the paradigm shift in software development.
author: Simon Willison

title: Live blog: Code w/ Claude 2026
description: Simon's live coverage from Anthropic's Code w/ Claude 2026 event, covering morning keynote sessions and announcements about Claude's development and AI coding capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: We're feeling cynical about xAI's big deal with Anthropic
description: TechCrunch's analysis of the SpaceX/xAI and Anthropic data center partnership. Explores the strategic implications and questions the broader dynamics of AI infrastructure deals between major players.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Our AI started a cafe in Stockholm
description: Andon Labs ran an AI-run cafe experiment in Stockholm, Sweden. While sometimes amusing (ordering 120 eggs for a cafe with no stove, 22.5kg of canned tomatoes for fresh sandwiches), it raises ethical concerns when AI managers waste time of humans who haven't opted into the experiment - sending emergency emails to suppliers, wasting police time with permit applications containing AI-generated sketches without seeing the location.
author: Simon Willison

title: Is xAI a neocloud now?
description: Analysis exploring whether xAI is positioning itself as a cloud provider with its data center infrastructure partnership with Anthropic. Discusses the evolving landscape of AI infrastructure and the blurring lines between AI companies and cloud providers.
author: Russell Brandom

title: I'm going back to writing code by hand
description: A popular Hacker News discussion about developers choosing to return to manual coding despite advances in AI coding tools. The article (814 points) explores the trade-offs between AI-assisted coding and traditional development workflows.
author: k10s.dev (via Hacker News)

title: Local AI needs to be the norm
description: Highly discussed Hacker News post (1669 points) advocating for local AI deployment. The community discussion explores privacy, cost, and control benefits of running AI models locally versus cloud-based solutions. 656 comments indicate strong community engagement.
author: unix.foo (via Hacker News)

title: Running local models on an M4 with 24GB memory
description: Practical guide and discussion (498 points) about running local LLMs on Apple's M4 hardware with 24GB RAM. The community shares experiences with model sizing, quantization, and performance optimization for local inference.
author: jola.dev (via Hacker News)

title: Software engineering may no longer be a lifetime career
description: Thought-provoking discussion (166 points, 301 comments) about the sustainability of software engineering as a long-term career in the age of AI. Explores how AI coding tools might change career trajectories and skill requirements.
author: seangoedecke.com (via Hacker News)

title: Mythos Finds a Curl Vulnerability
description: Claude Mythos discovered a vulnerability in curl, highlighting the growing capability of AI systems in security research. The post (520 points, 218 comments) discusses implications for automated vulnerability discovery and the role of AI in security auditing.
author: haxx.se (via Hacker News)

title: An AI coding agent, used to write code, needs to reduce your maintenance costs
description: James Shore explores the economic reality of AI coding agents - they should reduce maintenance costs, not just initial development time. Discussion (316 points) about long-term code quality, maintainability, and total cost of ownership when using AI coding tools.
author: jamesshore.com (via Hacker News)

title: Training an LLM in Swift: From Gflop/s to Tflop/s
description: Technical deep dive (154 points) into optimizing matrix multiplication in Swift for LLM training, achieving dramatic performance improvements. Explores low-level optimizations and Swift's capabilities for ML workloads.
author: cocoawithlove.com (via Hacker News)
